+package binding

+import (
+	"io"

+
+	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
+)
+
+type bsonBinding struct{}
+
+func (bsonBinding) Name() string {
+	return "bson"
+}
+
+func (b bsonBinding) Bind(req *http.Request, obj any) error {
+	buf, err := io.ReadAll(req.Body)

+	return bson.Unmarshal(body, obj)

+package render

+// BSON contains the given interface object.
+type BSON struct {

+}
+

+	}
+	return err
+}

+}

@laurentcau Please take a look.

In Hijack(), `w.size` is set to 0 (marking the response as written) before verifying the underlying ResponseWriter supports `http.Hijacker`. When the underlying writer does not support hijacking and you return `http.ErrNotSupported`, this side effect prevents later `WriteHeader` calls from changing the status (because `Written()` becomes true), which can break common fallback paths (e.g., try hijack, then send an HTTP error response). Consider only updating `w.size` (and thus `Written()`) after confirming hijacker support, and ideally only after a successful hijack call.

This assertion enforces that `Hijack()` sets `Written()` even when it returns `http.ErrNotSupported`. If Hijack is adjusted to avoid mutating writer state on unsupported/failed hijack attempts (so handlers can still set a status and write a fallback HTTP response), this test should be updated to reflect that expected behavior (e.g., `Written()` should remain false in the not-supported case).
